monthlyGoalPlanner.title: MONTHLY GOAL PLANNER
monthlyGoalPlanner.heading: LET'S BEGIN SETTING YOUR MONTHLY GOALS!
monthlyGoalPlanner.subheading: Now that you've learned how the goal-setting feature works, here's a summary before you get started.
monthlyGoalPlanner.card1Desc: Dedicate 20-30 minutes to choose ibadat practices that align with your aspirations. Cherish this time as a chance to deepen your connection with Allah (SWT) and set meaningful intentions.
monthlyGoalPlanner.card2Desc: Before adding a goal to your plan, tap each option to learn more. This helps you understand its purpose and importance, so you can choose goals that align with your spiritual priorities.
monthlyGoalPlanner.card3Desc: Select and save goals individually, giving you the freedom to pause and return anytime. With progress saved, you can explore options at your own pace for a stress-free, thoughtful experience.
monthlyGoalPlanner.card4Title: Confirm Goals and Begin Your 4-Week Cycle
monthlyGoalPlanner.card4Desc: After selecting goals, confirm them to start your 4-week cycle the next day. You'll have the entire 4 weeks to achieve them, helping you track progress and build consistency.
monthlyGoalPlanner.card5Desc: Once confirmed, goals can't be edited and remain locked for 4 weeks, promoting commitment to your targets and supporting a mindful, fulfilling spiritual routine.
monthlyGoalPlanner.card6Desc: Set new goals as your 4-week cycle nears its end. Don't worry-we'll send a reminder! If you don't update them, your current goals will automatically renew for another 4 weeks.
monthlyGoalPlanner.cycleStartDescription: Choose the day you'd like to begin your commitment. You'll have 4 weeks (28 days) from the date to complete your goals.
monthlyGoalPlanner.cycleStartFooterStart: Your 28-day goal cycle will run from

tahayyat-ul-wudhu.title: TAHIYYAT-UL-WUDHU
tahayyat-ul-wudhu.description: A two-rak'ah Sunnah prayer performed right after completing wudhu. It serves to honor the purification process and prepare us for further prayer
tahayyat-ul-wudhu.heroTitle: A Small Deed that Earns a Massive Reward
steps: Step 1: Perform Wudhu (Ablution) - Ensure you have completed your Wudhu before starting the prayer.
Step 2: Find a Clean and Quiet Place - Choose a clean and quiet place to perform the prayer, preferably facing the Qibla.
Step 3: Make the Intention (Niyyah) - Formulate the intention in your heart to perform two rak'ahs of Tahiyyat Al-Wudhu.
Step 4: Perform Two Rak'ahs - Pray two normal rak'ahs of prayer, reciting Surah Al-Fatihah and another surah in each rak'ah.
Step 5: Conclude with Salam - End the prayer with the salam to the right and then to the left.

fiveDailyPrayers.title: The 5 Daily Prayers
fiveDailyPrayers.description: The five obligatory prayers, most beloved to Allah, structure our day when prayed on time, instilling discipline and deepening our gratitude
fiveDailyPrayers.heroTitle: The Pillar of Faith and Key to Paradise
steps: Step 1: Be Mindful of the Time - Know the exact window of each obligatory prayer (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha).
Step 2: Attain State of Purity - Perform proper Wudhu (or Ghusl if required) prior to the prayer.
Step 3: Face the Qibla - Align yourself towards the Holy Kaaba in Makkah.
Step 4: Perform the Prayer with Khushu - Pray with complete focus, humility, and tranquility.
Step 5: Keep Consistency - Track and commit to completing all five daily prayers on time every single day.

sunnahRawatib.title: Sunnah Rawatib
sunnahRawatib.description: Aligns with the Prophet's (PBUH) sunnah and provides opportunities to compensate any shortcomings in obligatory prayers
steps: Step 1: Learn the Rawatib Prayers - The 12 rak'ahs: 2 before Fajr, 4 before Dhuhr, 2 after Dhuhr, 2 after Maghrib, and 2 after Isha.
Step 2: Pray Before/After Obligatory prayers - Offer these Sunnah prayers immediately before or after their respective Fard prayers.
Step 3: Maintain Focus - Give these voluntary prayers the same devotion and respect as obligatory ones.
Step 4: Track Progress - Strive to complete all 12 rak'ahs daily to unlock the promised reward.

thayyat-ul-masjid.title: THAYYAT-UL-MASJID
thayyat-ul-masjid.description: A two-rak’ah prayer performed upon entering the mosque, honoring its sanctity and seeking Allah’s blessings, guidance, and mercy
steps: Step 1: Enter the Mosque with Respect - Step in with your right foot first, reciting the invocation for entering the mosque.
Step 2: Form Intention (Niyyah) - Intend to pray two rak'ahs greeting the mosque before sitting down.
Step 3: Perform Two Rak'ahs - Pray the two rak'ahs with focus and tranquility.
Step 4: Complete Before Sitting - Ensure you pray these two rak'ahs immediately upon entering before you sit down.

missedPastPrayers.title: Missed Past Prayers
missedPastPrayers.description: Many of us have neglected obligatory prayers for weeks, months, or even years. Fulfilling these overdue prayers is a testament to our renewed commitment to Allah
steps: Step 1: Calculate Your Overdue Prayers - Make an honest estimate of the number of missed prayers you need to make up (Qada).
Step 2: Establish a Feasible Schedule - Plan to pray one or two make-up prayers alongside every current obligatory prayer daily.
Step 3: Remain Patient and Consistent - Compounding consistency over time is the best path to clear your spiritual debt.
Step 4: Keep Track of Your Progress - Log each completed Qada prayer to stay motivated and witness your progress.

duhaPrayer.title: Duha Prayer
duhaPrayer.description: It is performed in sets of 2 rak'ahs anytime from approximately 15-20 minutes after sunrise until about 10-15 minutes before the Dhuhr prayer
duhaPrayer.heroTitle: The Prayer of the Repentant and Charity for Joints
steps: Step 1: Wait for Sunrise - Allow 15-20 minutes to pass after sunrise before commencing the Duha prayer.
Step 2: Choose Rak'ahs - You can pray from 2 to 8 rak'ahs, in sets of two.
Step 3: Focus on Sincerity - Make the Niyyah in your heart to pray the Duha prayer.
Step 4: Complete Before Dhuhr - Complete your prayer before the sun reaches its zenith (about 10-15 minutes before Dhuhr).

tawbaPrayer.title: Tawba Prayer
tawbaPrayer.description: Also known as the repentance prayer in English, the Tawbah prayer is a sincere 2 rak'ah prayer to seek forgiveness from Allah for our sins
tawbaPrayer.heroTitle: A Sincere Return to Allah's Mercy
steps: Step 1: Perform Wudhu Beautifully - Wash yourself thoroughly, paying attention to the Sunnah steps of Wudhu.
Step 2: Make Sincere Intention - Deeply intend to seek Allah's forgiveness for your errors.
Step 3: Pray Two Rak'ahs - Pray two rak'ahs with absolute humility and focus.
Step 4: Beseech Allah's Forgiveness - In sujud or after salam, sincerely ask Allah to pardon you, promising to stay away from the sin.

istikharah.title: Istikharah Prayer
istikharah.description: A two rak'ah prayer performed to seek guidance from Allah when faced with a decision. It helps us make choices that align with our faith and best interests
steps: Step 1: Identify Your Dilemma - Have a specific decision or choice in mind.
Step 2: Pray Two Rak'ahs - Pray two voluntary non-obligatory rak'ahs.
Step 3: Recite the Istikharah Du'a - Recite the beautiful prophetic supplication after completing the prayer.
Step 4: Trust in Allah's Decree - Move forward with the best option, trusting that Allah will guide you to what is beneficial.

shukrPrayer.title: Shukr Prayer
shukrPrayer.description: The Gratitude Prayer (Shukr) is a 2-rak'ah act of thanks to Allah for His countless blessings. It fosters positivity by inspiring recognition of His generosity
steps: Step 1: Reflect on Blessings - Think about the specific blessing or overall goodness Allah has gifted you.
Step 2: Form Intention (Niyyah) - Intend to pray two rak'ahs purely in gratitude (Shukr) to Allah.
Step 3: Pray Two Rak'ahs - Perform two rak'ahs of voluntary prayer.
Step 4: Offer Heartfelt Praises - Spend time in prostration or after Salam praising and thanking Allah.

qiyamalLail.title: Qiyam al-Lail
qiyamalLail.description: Night prayers, performed between Isha and Fajr, are most beloved after obligatory prayers, fostering spiritual growth and inviting Allah’s mercy and blessings
qiyamalLail.heroTitle: The Secret Light in the Darkness of Night
steps: Step 1: Pray After Isha - You can pray Qiyam anytime between the conclusion of Isha prayer and the dawn of Fajr.
Step 2: Choose Your Style - Commit to every night or keep it flexible based on your weekly routine.
Step 3: Stand in Devotion - Pray sets of 2 rak'ahs. Recite the Quran slowly and thoughtfully.
Step 4: Track Tahajjud - Optionally wake up in the last third of the night for Tahajjud to seek the ultimate virtuous time.
Step 5: Conclude with Witr - Conclude your night prayers with one or three rak'ahs of Witr.

quran-listening.title: Quran Listening
quran-listening.description: Listening to the Quran brings tranquility, shields from evil, alleviates stress, enhances recitation, and refines tajweed skills, fostering spiritual growth
quran-listening.heroTitle: Opening the Heart to Divine Melody
steps: Step 1: Eliminate Distractions - Find a quiet spot and put away devices or background noises.
Step 2: Select a Beautiful Recitation - Pick a Qari whose voice moves your heart and helps you focus.
Step 3: Listen with Humility and Silence - Follow the instruction in the Quran: 'When the Quran is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy.'
Step 4: Contemplate the Meanings - Follow along with translation if available, allowing the verses to soothe your mind.

quran-recitation.title: Quran Recitation
quran-recitation.description: Reciting the Quran multiplies rewards, refines pronunciation, deepens understanding, and softens hearts, fostering a profound connection with Allah
quran-recitation.heroTitle: The Prophet's Legacy and Spiritual Nourishment
steps: Step 1: Clear Your Intentions - Recite purely for the sake of Allah and to earn His pleasure.
Step 2: Start with Isti'adhah and Basmalah - Seek refuge in Allah from Satan and begin in His name.
Step 3: Recite with Tartee - Recite in a measured, calm pace, not rushing through the words.
Step 4: Commit to a Daily Portion - Strive to recite at least one page or a few verses daily to stay connected.

quran-memorization.title: Quran Memorization
quran-memorization.description: Every word we memorize elevates our rank in Paradise, grants intercession for others, sharpens the mind, and enhances comprehension of the Quran
quran-memorization.heroTitle: Carrying the Divine Word in Your Chest
steps: Step 1: Choose a Small Portion - Start with small sections, e.g., one verse or a short surah.
Step 2: Understand the Meaning - Read the translation and simple Tafsir first to aid memory.
Step 3: Repeat Meticulously - Recite the same verse repeatedly until you can recall it smoothly without looking.
Step 4: Revise regularly - Constantly review previously memorized verses to keep them fresh.

qauran-tajweed.title: QURAN TAJWEED
qauran-tajweed.description: Tajweed perfects Quranic recitation as revealed to the Prophet (PBUH), preserving its authentic pronunciation, rhythm, and melody while deepening understanding
steps: Step 1: Learn the Basic Rules - Start with clear rules like Noon Sakinah, Meem Sakinah, and letters of prolongation (Madd).
Step 2: Listen to Expert Reciters - Listen to standard recitations (like Sheikh Al-Husary) to mimic proper articulation.
Step 3: Practice with a Teacher - Correct your mistakes by reciting to a qualified teacher whenever possible.
Step 4: Apply Tajweed to Daily Recitation - Consciously apply the rules to every verse you recite in your daily prayers.

missed-fasts.title: Missed Ramadan Fasts
missed-fasts.description: Fulfilling missed obligatory fasts is a duty that reflects devotion, demonstrates discipline, and upholds our commitment to Allah’s commands
steps: Step 1: Count Your Missed Days - List down the number of obligatory Ramadan fasts you missed due to travel, illness, or other valid reasons.
Step 2: Set the Intention - Formulate the intention (Niyyah) to make up a missed Ramadan fast before dawn.
Step 3: Observe the Fast - Abstain from food, drink, and invalidators from dawn to sunset.
Step 4: Mark Your Completion - Break your fast with dates or water, and log it to track your remaining makeup days.

dawood-fasts.title: The Fast of Prophet Dawood
dawood-fasts.description: These fasts are observed by fasting every other day, reflecting Prophet Dawood's (PBUH) devotion and resilience, and serving as a model of piety
dawood-fasts.heroTitle: The Most Beloved Fasting to Allah
steps: Step 1: Understand the Routine - Fast one day and eat the next, consistently alternating.
Step 2: Form Sincere Niyyah - Make the intention for the Sunnah fast prior to dawn.
Step 3: Maintain Strength and Health - Ensure your nutrition on non-fasting days supports this high level of spiritual endurance.
Step 4: Keep Consistency - Maintain the alternate-day cycle for the duration of your goal period.

monday-and-thursday-fasts.title: Monday & Thursday Fasts
monday-and-thursday-fasts.description: These fasts follow the Prophet's (PBUH) Sunnah, deepen devotion to Allah, promote well-being, and offer profound spiritual purification and self-discipline
steps: Step 1: Pick the Days - Identify Mondays and Thursdays in your calendar.
Step 2: Set Niyyah - Make your intention to observe the Sunnah fast before Fajr.
Step 3: Practice Gratitude - Remember that deeds are presented to Allah on these days, and fasting is a beautiful state to be in.
Step 4: Share the Joy - Break your fast with family or friends to foster a warm Islamic environment.

white-days-fasts.title: White Days Fasts
white-days-fasts.description: Fasting on the 13th, 14th, and 15th of each Islamic month deepens connection with Allah, nurtures discipline, and inspires profound spiritual growth and self-reflection
steps: Step 1: Track the Hijri Calendar - Find the 13th, 14th, and 15th days of the current Islamic month.
Step 2: Intend the Fast - Formulate intention for these Sunnah (Ayyam al-Beed) fasts.
Step 3: Abstain and Purify - Fast faithfully during these three consecutive days.
Step 4: Reflect on Rewards - Fasting these three days earns the reward of fasting the entire month.

missed-zakat.title: Missed Zakat
missed-zakat.description: Fulfilling missed Zakat is a sacred obligation that purifies wealth, restores social equity, and reaffirms a believer’s responsibility to support society’s welfare
steps: Step 1: Assess Missed Years - Estimate the years or amounts of obligatory Zakat you neglected to pay.
Step 2: Calculate the Dues - Calculate 2.5% of your qualifying surplus wealth for each missed year.
Step 3: Direct to Eligible Recipients - Ensure the funds are distributed to the eight categories specified in the Quran.
Step 4: Complete Promptly - Pay off your outstanding Zakat to fulfill this crucial pillar of Islam.

kafarah-for-breaking-fasts.title: Kafarah for Breaking Fasts
kafarah-for-breaking-fasts.description: A form of sadaqah to atone for broken fasts or oaths, requiring feeding or clothing those in need as prescribed
steps: Step 1: Determine the Atonement Required - Consult scholars to identify your specific Kafarah (e.g., feeding 60 poor people or fasting for 60 days).
Step 2: Prepare the Charity - Calculate the cost of meals or clothing if feeding/clothing is your assigned atonement.
Step 3: Distribute Sincerely - Hand over the food or clothing to deserving, needy recipients.
Step 4: Seek Forgiveness - Combine your material atonement with a sincere repentance to Allah.

fidya.title: Fidya
fidya.description: A form of sadaqah that allows those unable to fast due to illness or age to stay spiritually connected by feeding one person per missed fast day
steps: Step 1: Count Missed Ramadan Days - Track each day of fasting missed due to persistent illness, old age, or pregnancy.
Step 2: Calculate the Cost - Standard Fidya is feeding one needy person two meals (or equivalent cost) per missed day.
Step 3: Partner with Charities - Route your Fidya through reliable channels to reach those in need.
Step 4: Keep Record - Track your payments to ensure every missed fast is fully accounted for.

lilah-donations.title: Lilah Donations
lilah-donations.description: Lillah, derived from the Arabic term 'for Allah', is a pure form of sadaqah driven by a sincere desire to please Allah, fostering devotion and selflessness among Muslims
lilah-donations.heroTitle: Giving Purely for the Sake of Allah
steps: Step 1: Purify Your Intention - Ensure your donation is purely to seek Allah's pleasure, completely free from vanity.
Step 2: Find Deserving Causes - Look for mosques, Islamic centers, or humanitarian funds requiring support.
Step 3: Donate Secretly - Whenever possible, give your donation secretly to safeguard your sincerity.
Step 4: Make Supplication - Ask Allah to accept this small token and to bless your remaining wealth.

volunteering-services.title: Volunteering Services
volunteering-services.description: As Muslims, offering our time and skills without expecting any compensation is a noble act and a profound expression of faith, bringing us closer to Allah
volunteering-services.heroTitle: Serving Creation to Please the Creator
steps: Step 1: Identify Your Talents - Think about how your skills (teaching, cooking, organizing, coding) can benefit the community.
Step 2: Dedicate Free Time - Set aside a few hours in your month specifically for voluntary services.
Step 3: Help Local Organizations - Offer your time to local mosques, charity drives, soup kitchens, or youth clubs.
Step 4: Practice Kindness - Treat everyone you serve with the utmost respect, smile, and warm manners.

sadaqah-jariyah.title: Sadaqah Jariyah
sadaqah-jariyah.description: This form of Sadaqah is the most rewarding—it’s the gift that keeps giving, offering endless blessings and rewards in this life and the hereafter
sadaqah-jariyah.heroTitle: The Gift that Keeps Giving Beyond Life
steps: Step 1: Choose a Long-Term Project - Select projects like water wells, planting trees, building mosques, or sponsoring Islamic education.
Step 2: Commit Funds - Dedicate a portion of your wealth to contribute to these high-impact projects.
Step 3: Involve Family - Partner with relatives or friends to sponsor projects together.
Step 4: Make Du'a for Continuity - Supplicate that this project remains operational, continuously benefiting others and storing rewards for your hereafter.
